findings.title: JWT Signature Verification Missing - Authentication Bypass
findings.impact: Complete authentication bypass allowing attackers to forge any JWT token and impersonate any user without knowing the signing secret
findings.evidence: Function uses jwt.decode() without jwt.verify(); no secret key validation. Line 6: const claims = jwt.decode(bearer); Attacker can create JWT with arbitrary payload and send it with any signature
findings.recommendation: Replace jwt.decode(bearer) with jwt.verify(bearer, SECRET_KEY) to validate token signature. This requires a secret key to be configured and used for both token signing and verification

findings.title: SQL Injection in ORDER BY Parameter
findings.impact: Arbitrary SQL command execution allowing data exfiltration, modification, or destruction of database tables
findings.evidence: Line 24 directly interpolates req.query.order into SQL template: const rows = await db.query(`SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE owner_id = $1 ORDER BY ${order}`, [req.user.id]); Parameter sourced from user input with no sanitization. Contrast: /payments endpoint at line 31 correctly uses whitelist SORTABLE filtering
findings.recommendation: Apply whitelist validation like the /payments endpoint: define const SORTABLE = {'created_at': 'created_at', 'updated_at': 'updated_at'} and use const column = SORTABLE[req.query.order] || 'created_at'; Use column in query instead of direct interpolation

findings.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Invoice Notes - Unescaped HTML
findings.impact: Arbitrary JavaScript execution in user browser context allowing cookie theft, session hijacking, credential harvesting, and malware injection
findings.evidence:
Function invoiceNote() at line 5 renders note without escaping: return `
${note}
`. Module imports escape-html at line 1 and uses it correctly in customerName() at line 10, but omits escaping in invoiceNote(). User-controlled note content flows directly into HTML template
findings.recommendation:
Apply escapeHtml() to the note parameter: function invoiceNote(note) { return `
${escapeHtml(note)}
`; } This matches the secure pattern already demonstrated in customerName()

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via Unvalidated HTTP Redirects
findings.impact: Ability to access internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, and private network resources by chaining HTTP redirects through attacker-controlled URLs
findings.evidence: Function fetchLogo() at line 6 uses fetch(url, { redirect: 'follow' }) allowing arbitrary redirect chains. Contrast: fetchAsset() at line 14 correctly uses { redirect: 'error' } to reject redirects. Attacker can POST logoUrl: 'https://attacker.com/step1' which redirects to 'http://localhost:6379' (Redis) or '169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/' (AWS credentials)
findings.recommendation: Change { redirect: 'follow' } to { redirect: 'error' } in fetchLogo() function. Additionally, validate the parsed URL hostname against a whitelist before fetching, similar to the whitelist pattern used in fetchAsset() with the ALLOWED set
